targets.title: Malformed dist files crash in the new archDistArchFree; flags not inherited
targets.why: Right: well-formed 'dist' files now load, save and reload (dist_ok, dist_sub, dist_subsub: ret=0, no report), the inner Arch is allocated, the new archDistArchFree() is registered and renamed in module.h, and matching routines make 'dist' usable inside 'sub' ('sub 2 0 1 dist 2 cmplt 4' loads and round-trips). This settles the 7.0.17 design question: he keeps 'dist' as a loadable class and owns the inner Arch (our option A). Incomplete: (1) archDistArchFree() (arch_dist.c:161-164) does not check archptr->archptr, which is set only on success (arch_dist.c:111), so every malformed 'dist' file crashes in the clean-up that archLoad() performs: 'dist abc' and 'dist 2 cmplt abc' -> 'arch.c:173:15: runtime error: member access within null pointer of type struct Arch ... #1 _SCOTCHarchDistArchFree arch_dist.c:162' then SEGV; a plain-build malloc-failure sweep crashes dist_ok.tgt at #3 and dist_sub/dist_subsub at every failure from #3 on; (2) the inner Arch (arch_dist.c:101) is not archInit()ed, so a nested 'dist'/'sub' whose loading fails frees garbage ('dist 2 dist 3 cmplt abc', 'dist 2 sub 3 0' -> 0xbebebebe); (3) a loaded 'dist' does not inherit ARCHVAR/ARCHPART from its inner architecture, which archDistArchBuild() does (arch_dist.c:186): 'dist 2 varcmplt' reports var=0 size=1 and gmap maps all 16 vertices of m4x4 onto one domain, while 'varcmplt' alone spreads them; (4) crloval < 1 is accepted ('dist 0 cmplt 4' loads; kgraphInit() rejects it only under SCOTCH_DEBUG_KGRAPH2, kgraph.c:98-103); (5) archDistArchBuild() still copies ARCHFREE from the original architecture, which it does not own: latent double free (no caller). Companion test: 0d878bdd adds 'gmap bump.grf data/sub_dist_mesh2d.tgt' ('sub 5 2 3 6 7 9 dist 2 mesh2d 4 4') to check_prog_gmap and CMake; it passes on the patched 32/64-bit trees.
targets.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 0003 had the NULL-tolerant free, archInit(), flag inheritance, crloval >= 1 and the ARCHFREE mask; his has the matching routines (archDistMatchInit/Exit/Mate, ArchDistMatch in ArchMatchDummy), which ours did not and which are a real improvement. Rebased 0003 keeps his structure (inner Arch published after success, his 'bad input (1)/(2)' messages, his variable name dstarchptr) and adds only the five missing pieces. He also added a regression test (0d878bdd), which ours did not.

commits.subject: Bugfix: abort cleanly when cannot start thread system [report R. Perry]

targets.title: Thread creation failure with launched slaves still hangs; master never joins start-up barrier
targets.why: Right: desctab is now freed (:147) and the lock features are destroyed even when no slave was launched (Exit3 :193-194), which fixes the leak for FAIL_AT=1; threadWaitBarrier1 reads thrdnbr under the lock, which a reduced count needs. Wrong: the reduced count (:145, thrdnbr = thrdnum) includes the master, but the master never takes part in the start-up barrier on the failure path, so the barrier can never complete (slave positions are 1..thrdnum-1); the in-loop 're-check' at :333 can therefore never fire. Exit3's spin (:186-190) counts barrier arrivals as terminations, exits early and destroys the cond/mutex with waiters: glibc blocks forever in pthread_cond_destroy (same hang as 7.0.17, new place); with other libcs/TSan the slaves are left parked on destroyed primitives inside a ThreadContext that contextThreadInit2 frees (common_context.c:202): use after free (TSan report). Also :145 writes thrdnbr without the lock while slaves read it under the lock (data race; 'volatile' added to common_thread.h does not make it race-free). Even with a slave-only count (thrdnum - 1) Exit3 would stay racy: barrnbr can equal the slave count from barrier arrivals stored before the reduction, before the last slave resets it. Typo 'shutdow' copied from Exit2.
targets.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 0002 did what is still missing: lock, reduce thrdnbr, master joins threadContextBarrier, then exits (the barrier resets barrnbr to 0, so the exit spin counts only terminations). His version is better on structure (dedicated Exit3 that always destroys the lock features, so no special case for thrdnum == 1; barrier reading thrdnbr under lock). The rebased 0002 keeps all of his code and adds only the locked reduction and the master's barrier call (3 lines): best of both.

targets.title: Sub-architecture terminal checks now unconditional, but empty lists still accepted
targets.why: Right: the checks are now unconditional (arch_sub.c:396, 442-446), the 0xbebebebe archExit() of 7.0.17 is gone, archSubArchFree() skips NULL fields (arch_sub.c:195-202), and the inner Arch is now owned by the body from the start of Build (arch_sub.c:383), i.e. the same ownership protocol as our 0001. Wrong: (1) the newly unconditional fail1 path (arch_sub.c:448-452) frees termtab, which was already recorded in the body at arch_sub.c:425, so archSubArchFree() (called by archLoad() or by SCOTCH_archExit() after a failed SCOTCH_archSub()) frees it again: 'sub 2 0 99 cmplt 4' and 'sub 2 0 0 cmplt 4' -> 'AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free ... #1 _SCOTCHarchSubArchFree arch_sub.c:202 #2 _SCOTCHarchLoad arch.c:216; freed by ... _SCOTCHarchSubArchBuild arch_sub.c:451' (new defect PS3-G01-1: in 7.0.17 release builds this path did not exist). Incomplete: (2) the inner Arch allocated at arch_sub.c:112 is still never archInit()ed, so when its own loading fails, archLoad() calls its class free hook on an uninitialized body: 'sub 2 0 1 sub 3 0' -> 'arch.c:173:15: runtime error: member access within misaligned address 0xbebebebebebebebe' via archSubArchFree arch_sub.c:196; 'sub 2 0 1 tleaf abc' -> SEGV in free; malloc-failure sweep on a plain build: sub_sub.tgt crashes for failed malloc #5-9, sub_tleaf.tgt and sub_cmpltw.tgt for #5; (3) the fail2 path (arch_sub.c:472-484) frees only the first tree block, so the 'internal error (2)' and 'cannot create sub-architecture (2)' paths still leak the coarser blocks, and in the SCOTCH_archSub() path the published termtab is leaked unless the caller calls SCOTCH_archExit(); (4) vnumnbr == 0 is still accepted by both the loader ('termnbr < 0', arch_sub.c:92) and Build (arch_sub.c:396), so 'sub 0 cmplt 4' reaches memAllocGroup() with size 2*0-1 < 0 ('AddressSanitizer: requested allocation size 0xffffffffffffffec' from arch_sub.c:403); (5) single-terminal sub-architectures other than vertex 0 (PS2-G01-1) are not addressed: they now fail with 'internal error (2)' instead of crashing. Cosmetic: comment typo 'sob-architecture' (arch_sub.c:122).
targets.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 0001 used the same ownership protocol but (a) archInit()ed the inner Arch, (b) published the body fields only on success and (c) freed the whole tree chain once on every late failure: all three are what upstream still lacks, and (b) is exactly what prevents his new double free. His version is better in one respect: the archDomTerm() check is now unconditional (ours folded it into the message chain too). Rebased 0001 = his code + (a), (b), (c); rebased 0002 = the 'vnumnbr < 1' remainder of our 0002.
